summary: The unversioned (format 0) files as the first published releases (0.0.2 to 0.0.11, nightlies included) create them: the catalog has no shell_coverage table, guidance has no supervisor_planning_attempts table or supervisor_planning_project index, and its default settings row is the legacy reminder document. thread-settings and access are identical to 0.0.27's.
choice: The oldest published layout and the one furthest from 0.0.27: it lacks the two later table additions (catalog shell_coverage since 0.0.15; guidance supervisor_planning_attempts and its index since 0.0.12) and keeps the legacy guidance settings document (written until 0.0.13-nightly) whose retired reminder fields 0.0.27 leaves in the row, unread. No published release lacks a column that a later release adds with ALTER TABLE: every ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN executed on a file created by a release is the unconditional-in-practice episodes.object_id / notices.rule_generation / notices.settings_generation trio, which every release ran on its own new file; the conditional ALTERs (expected_revision, review_misses, activation_ordinal, untracked_count, read_item_id, active) only ever applied to pre-release prototype files, never to a release's. This layout therefore exercises the later additions as table additions, and both fixtures carry the ALTER-appended column text in sqlite_master. No published release had the pre-'main-v1' project-scoped prototype (supervisor_project_bindings, supervisor_monitor_project_clock, no supervisor_scope_version): it existed only in unpublished development builds of 2026-10-13/14 (commits 53f0a5e and 12f8746), before the first public version 0.0.2 (RELEASING.md: earlier prototype versions were never published). Every release writes supervisor_scope_version='main-v1' when it first builds its supervision stores, so it is not frozen here.

producedBy.note: Linear history. Tags are read with read-only git show; 0.0.27 is commit 4ce025945b9cc62864b0db3d8c8249d4e957b6b5 (Release 0.0.27, #93), untagged in this clone. No release writes PRAGMA user_version or application_id, so each file is format 0.

provenance.method: Each statement's text was copied from the string literal(s) of the released source at the recorded lines (identifiers and bound parameters resolved as noted), and checked to be identical at every release listed in producedBy. Statements are in the order the released binary executed them on a new file; IF NOT EXISTS is part of the copied text. The schema files contain no comments; each statement ends with ';' directly after its last token, because SQLite keeps the text up to that token in sqlite_master.
provenance.lineRanges: per statement for the first (0.0.2) and last (0.0.11) release of the layout

statements.note: SESSION_TTL_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000 = 2592000000, concatenated into the CHECK constraint

statements: src/service-auth.ts: every open validates quick_check, journal_mode=delete, exactly the two tables (whitespace-insensitive schema text and table_info), at most 32 grants and 32 sessions, expires_at > issued_at and the 30 day session TTL; the file must be a regular 0600 file of at most 1 MiB

syntheticRows.label: synthetic fixture input, not old-binary output
contents: dashboard_login_grants: one pending single-use grant (5 minute TTL as auth forge issues it)
dashboard_login_sessions: two sessions at the 30 day TTL bound (expires_at - issued_at = 2592000000)
token_hash = sha256(token) in lowercase hex; the synthetic tokens are listed in the manifest (32 sequential bytes each, base64url), not credentials

syntheticData.label: synthetic fixture input, not old-binary output
syntheticData.statement: Every row is invented: identities are 'fixture-...' strings or zero-filled v4 UUIDs, texts are fixture prose, timestamps lie between 2026-10-20 and 2026-11-03. No row comes from a real installation, chat, credential or person.
syntheticData.readerAcceptance: Rows were written to pass the 0.0.27 readers' guards (the Schema guards of each store's rollout-scan decoder and the access validation); documents follow the key order of the released writers; documents the released writers changed with json_set/json_remove were computed with the same SQLite functions.

accessTokens.note: synthetic sign-in tokens (32 sequential bytes, base64url), not credentials; token_hash = sha256(token) lowercase hex

assumptions: thread-settings was first created with EXCLUDED_THREAD_IDS=fixture-thread-config-excluded (seed {"generation":1,"excludedThreadIds":["fixture-thread-config-excluded"]}); the rows file then sets the policy to generation 7 as six dashboard saves would.
The data directory and access/ are 0700 and every database file 0600, as src/db.ts preparePrivateFile and the access bootstrap leave them; the WAL files were checkpointed and removed by a clean stop.

access/workflow-mcp-token (the workflow MCP seed file the auth bootstrap writes beside login.sqlite3) is not a database and is not part of the fixture; the 0.0.27 auth service creates it when missing.

The expected dumps were computed from the frozen statements, not captured from files the published binaries wrote; their sqlite_master text is that of node v24.22.1 (SQLite 3.53.4), the runtime of every release image. Comparing them once with files a published binary of each layout creates (sqlite_master, table_info, user_version and journal mode per file) is a separate manual check.

Legacy and compact guidance settings defaults: {"generation":1,"guidancePaused":false,"monitoringPaused":false,"allowFollowupRace":false,"verifiedServerVersion":null,"model":"gpt-6-luna","reasoning":"high","dailyTokenBudget":100000,"evidenceHours":24,"maxAnchorAgeSeconds":60} (0.0.2 .. 0.0.13-nightly) and {"generation":1,"evidenceHours":24} (0.0.13 .. 0.0.27).

generation.tool: a throwaway generator outside the repository (not shipped, not run by tests): read-only git show of the released sources, node:crypto for hashes, an in-memory node:sqlite for json_set results
generation.expectedDumps: computed once by executing <name>.schema.sql then <name>.rows.sql with node:sqlite DatabaseSync (node v24.22.1, SQLite 3.53.4) into a new file after PRAGMA journal_mode=<journalMode>, closing it, and reading it back immutable: sqlite_master ordered by type and name, the creation order, PRAGMA table_info per table, row counts, PRAGMA user_version and the journal mode of the file header
generation.never: These files are frozen. They are never regenerated from today's schema constants, serializers or factories; a new layout gets a new directory.
